_source.status: House rule. Original content, not from Mausritter.
_source.rationale: Mausritter has no shops or services table and no availability-by-size chart. The SRD gives only scattered hooks, quoted in each entry's srdBasis field. Everything here beyond those quotes is this project's invention and is not official Mausritter content.
_source.licence: Original work by the mausritter-tools authors, released with the repository.
_source.warning: Safe to edit by hand. Unlike the files in ../srd/, this is not regenerated by the importer.

priceVarianceNote: Each shop shifts its prices by up to this much either way, so the same item costs a little more in one settlement than another. Mice mostly deal in barter and IOUs anyway.

services.name: General store
services.srdBasis: Mouse-made tools are "available in most mouse settlements".
services.blurb: Rope, bedrolls, buckets and chalk, stacked to the rafters.

services.name: Victualler
services.srdBasis: The SRD prices meals, grand meals and travel rations, and puts a week of food and board at 20p.
services.blurb: Rations wrapped in waxed leaf, and a pot of something hot.

services.name: Smith and armourer
services.srdBasis: The armourer/blacksmith hireling has a Number of d2, and the SRD prices repairs at 10% of the item's cost per usage dot.
services.blurb: Sparks, sharpened needles, and usage dots ground back out for 10% a dot.

services.name: Chandler
services.srdBasis: The SRD lists torches, lanterns, oil, electric lanterns and batteries as purchasable light sources.
services.blurb: Torches by the bundle, and a lantern that has seen better tunnels.

services.name: Hireling hall
services.srdBasis: "In a mouse settlement, you can spend a day asking around for mice looking for work. The size of the settlement determines what types of hireling are available." The SRD never gives the mapping; the size gating used here is invented.
services.blurb: Mice loitering hopefully, waiting to be asked. WIL save or 20p to recruit.

services.name: Scavenger's stall
services.srdBasis: Human-made tools are "available in mouse settlements near human populations". This is the one service gated by geography rather than size.
services.blurb: Human leavings, dragged home and priced optimistically.

services.name: Clothier
services.srdBasis: The SRD prices poor, standard and noble clothing plus winter and waterproof cloaks.
services.blurb: Waxed cloaks for the road, and one noble outfit nobody here can afford.

services.name: Bank and safebox
services.srdBasis: "In a mouse settlement, pips and items can be stored in a bank or safebox. Your mouse must pay a fee of 1% of the value when retrieving."
services.blurb: Pips and heirlooms held safe. Retrieval costs 1% of the value.
services.serviceTerms: Storage is free. Retrieval costs 1% of the value stored.

services.name: Stables and transport
services.srdBasis: The SRD prices rabbit wagons, river rafts and pigeon flights per mouse, per hex.
services.blurb: A bad-tempered rabbit, a raft, and rates quoted per hex.

services.name: Apothecary
services.srdBasis: Extrapolated from the Industry table entry "Gardens of rare herbs. Drying racks are guarded" and the SRD's perfume and soap entries. Mausritter has no apothecary rules; treat the stock as flavour.
services.blurb: Bundles of drying herbs, and advice you did not ask for.

services.name: Sage's scriptorium
services.srdBasis: The scholar hireling has a Number of d2, and the SRD prices a blank book at 300p and a reading book at 600p.
services.blurb: Books at 300p blank and 600p written, and a scholar who will read them to you.

services.name: Jeweller
services.srdBasis: Extrapolated from the SRD's treasure values: gold ring 500p, jewelled pendant 400p, polished diamond 1000p, string of pearls 1500p.
services.blurb: Buys treasure at a hard price and sells it back at a harder one.
services.serviceTerms: Buys recovered treasure, typically at about half its listed value.

services.name: Curio dealer
services.srdBasis: "If unwanted, a fully charged spell can usually be sold for d6 x 100p in a settlement. A depleted spell's value is halved." Note the SRD only covers selling spells, never buying them, so a dealer who sells spells is entirely a house rule.
services.blurb: Will buy a spell off you for d6 x 100p. Selling one back is another matter.

Haggles ferociously, and enjoys it
Everything is dusted with flour
Keeps a beetle on a leash by the door
Will only trade, never take pips
Prices are chalked up and rubbed out hourly
Insists on telling you the history of each item
Deeply suspicious of outsiders
Offers tea before business, always
Half the stock is spoken for already
Sells at a loss and cannot explain why
Keeps the good stock hidden under the counter
Owes money to someone frightening
Runs the shop from a hammock
Counts pips three times, out loud
Extends credit to anyone with a sad story
Spotless, and smells of beeswax
Sleeps in the back and resents being woken
Discounts for anyone who admires the beetle-shell sign
Convinced a rival is stealing from them
